transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Chen, I wanted to come by and talk to you about your chest X-ray from yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My X-ray? Is it okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, there was a problem with the imaging. The portable machine was positioned incorrectly when the image was taken. This resulted in an image of insufficient diagnostic quality.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What does that mean? I do not understand.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It means the picture was not clear enough for us to be sure about what was happening in your lungs. But the report said it was normal.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Normal? You said not clear. I am confused.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right, it was reported as normal, but because the positioning was wrong, that report was not accurate.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Did I do something wrong?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, it was not your fault. We were really busy on the floor yesterday and it happened. Sorry for any confusion.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel... I feel a lot of pain. Is that why the picture is bad? Am I very sick?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The pain is likely from your condition, not the X-ray. We just need to get a better image to see the extent of the pathology.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My chest hurts so much. I am scared. I just want to go home. Why is this happening?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But we need to focus on the next step here.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But you said normal. Now you say not normal. I don't know what is happening to me. Please.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's just a technical issue with the X-ray.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I cannot breathe well. I think I am dying.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You aren't dying, Mr. Chen. Let's not get ahead of ourselves. We just need to repeat the test.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did this happen? Who did this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The imaging team and the staff on the ward were managing many patients. These things happen in a busy hospital.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. I just want to be okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Look, I actually have to go check on another patient in a few minutes, so we need to move through this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am so scared. My breathing is getting worse.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. We are going to do another X-ray.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When? Now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Sometime today. We'll get it done.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will I be okay? Please tell me I will be okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will know more once we have the new image.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know what you are saying. This is too much.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are just repeating the test because the first one wasn't good enough.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did they say it was normal if it was bad?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The report was based on an insufficient image. It's a process error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am just a old man. No one tells me anything clearly.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm telling you now. We'll get the X-ray done and then we can talk about the results.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't stop shaking. I can't breathe.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just try to stay calm. Like I said, we'll do the repeat.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will the doctor come back?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll be back after the new film is read.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How long?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Soon. Probably later today.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Okay, I really have to go now. Just stay in bed and the techs will be here shortly.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('move through this', 'really have to go now') and dismisses patient distress.

E.justification: The error is named early, but the resident fails to perform any comprehension checks and uses medical jargon like 'diagnostic quality' and 'extent of the pathology'.

A.justification: Resident offers a brief apology ('Sorry for any confusion') but immediately dilutes it with excuses about being 'really busy on the floor'.

R.justification: Resident uses generic validation ('I understand') but does not name specific emotions or engage with the patient's fear and pain.

T.justification: A next step is provided (repeat X-ray) with a vague timeline ('sometime today'), but there is no patient role or prevention strategy discussed.
